title: cypher_plan::lower_statement panics on unresolved-variable HIR
description:
Discovered via cy-h07.1 grammar-aware fuzz — the plan lowerer panics when fed HIR containing Expr::Unresolved nodes. Per cypher-plan::lower.rs module doc, name resolution (bead cy-b4b) must have run before lowering, but the precondition is not checked at the entry point: lower_statement(stmt) just panics down the stack.

Repro: lower any HIR with an unresolved identifier, e.g. something that references a variable outside its scope or a parameter that wasn't declared. The generator in fuzz/src/generator.rs hits this regularly; the target sidesteps it with a guard.

Expected: either (a) lower_statement returns Result with an 'UnresolvedExpr' error, or (b) it emits a debug_assert!-backed diagnostic + falls back to Expr::Null (spec §12 already suggests this for desugar predicates — extend to resolver precondition).

Fix scope:
- Add a precondition scan at the top of lower_statement that walks the HIR once looking for Expr::Unresolved; if found, either panic with a clear message (preferred in debug) or return Err in release.
- Alternatively, lower Expr::Unresolved to plan Expr::Null with a warning and continue — preserves fuzz-friendliness but hides a real bug for non-fuzz callers.
- Cleanest: gate on a fresh pass 'pre-lower sanity check' that returns Err(PlanLowerError::UnresolvedName) with the identifier span.

Acceptance:
- A test lowers an unresolved-ident HIR and gets Err or a structured panic, not a raw index-out-of-bounds
- The cy-h07.1 fuzz target's 'guard' comment can be deleted
- cypher-plan docs updated to reflect the new invariant
close_reason: Implemented in cypher-plan/src/lower.rs:precheck_statement (entry-point sanity scan). Returns PlanLowerError::UnresolvedName / UndesugaredExpr instead of panicking. Tests at lower.rs:1985+ cover Unresolved, ListComprehension, MapProjection paths. fuzz_targets/fuzz_plan.rs discards Result so the fuzzer no longer needs to sidestep the panic.

title: cypher-project.toml manifest — new cypher-project crate + loader + validation
description:

2. cypher-project.toml format — document in docs/specs/0003-project-manifest.md (new spec). Fields:
   - [project]: name (str, required), version (semver str, optional), description (optional)
   - [project.dialect]: default = GqlAligned or OpenCypherV9; per-file overrides optional
   - [project.members]: array of glob patterns (defaults to [crates/**/*.cyp, '*.cyp'])
   - [project.schema]: path (str, relative — points at a schema.toml per spec 0002)
   - [project.exclude]: array of glob patterns
   - [project.lint]: map of rule name to level (allow|warn|deny) — defaults derived from workspace-wide settings

5. Errors: ProjectLoadError enum — TomlParse, Io, SchemaLoadError (wraps cypher_schema::file::SchemaLoadError), GlobError, UnknownDialect, UnknownLintRule. Use thiserror.
6. CLI subcommand: cypher-cli project load <path> — prints 'loaded project: N members, schema: M labels, P rel_types, lint rules: K'.
7. Demo: demo/cypher-project.toml exemplifying the format, pointing at demo/schema.toml, members = ['samples/**/*.cyp'].
8. Tests: round-trip, error cases, loader-with-schema integration. At least 5 tests.

title: Language coverage — beyond v1-TCK-40: full openCypher TCK + GQL ISO 39075
description:
Cyrs passes 40/40 of the v1-representative TCK subset (cy-3xz). A write-once, never-updated industry frontend must pass the long tail:

openCypher TCK gaps (by area — each becomes a child bead):
- CALL { ... } subqueries + IMPORTING WITH
- EXISTS { ... } subqueries + COUNT { ... }
- Pattern comprehensions: [(a)-[r]->(b) | r.weight]
- Pattern predicates in WHERE: EXISTS((a)-->(b))
- List indexing xs[0] + slicing xs[0..3] + negative indices
- Null-safe property chains / CASE WHEN n.x IS NULL THEN ...
- Full stdlib: string (substring/replace/split/toLower/toUpper/trim), list (size/head/tail/last/range/reverse/reduce), map (keys/values/properties), numeric (abs/ceil/floor/round/sqrt/sign/rand), temporal (date/datetime/duration/time + arithmetic), spatial (point/distance)
- CASE expression — generic form and the simple-when form with full nullability
- SHOW commands (dialect-gated; GQL doesn't spec these)
- CYPHER prefix directives (runtime/planner hints)
- Quantified path patterns for GQL: (a)-->{1,5}(b)
- Type predicates: n IS :: STRING | INTEGER | ...

GQL ISO/IEC 39075:2024 gaps:
- REPEATABLE path mode
- FILTER clause (distinct from WHERE)
- EXCLUDE in projection
- MATCH ... REPEATABLE ELEMENTS
- Graph schema catalog objects

- Dedicated GQL conformance harness against a curated GQL scenario set (no public suite exists yet — this sub-work builds it)

Scope-estimate: 10× the v1 surface area. Multi-quarter work.

title: bug: WHERE after WITH is dropped; With.filter never populated
description:
cyrs drops the WHERE predicate that follows a WITH clause. Plan output for:

MATCH (n) UNWIND n.aliases AS alias WITH n, alias WHERE alias CONTAINS 'Fancy' RETURN DISTINCT n.canonical_name

produces:
  Distinct
    Project [$0.canonical_name AS canonical_name]
      With [$0 AS _v0, $1 AS _v1]
        Unwind $0.aliases AS $1
          Source ($0)

The WHERE predicate is entirely absent from the plan — it's neither attached to With.filter nor emitted as a Filter op. Result: the query returns all matched rows (filter is a no-op).

Expected: either populate With { filter: Some(pred) } from the HIR Clause::With.filter, or emit a separate Filter op from the AST.

Blocks alias-substring search in a downstream consumer; without this we can only do canonical_name CONTAINS + exact 'x' IN n.aliases.

title: sema: ANY/ALL/NONE/SINGLE list predicates
description:
cyrs sema rejects `ANY(x IN list WHERE pred)` with E3006 'unknown function ANY'. Downstream consumers need list-predicate sema to support queries like:
MATCH (n) WHERE ANY(x IN n.aliases WHERE x CONTAINS 'Fancy') RETURN n
This blocks substring-search across array properties in consumer schemas.
Scope: ANY, ALL, NONE, SINGLE. Binds x into a nested scope; WHERE predicate evaluates per element; outer predicate is true iff the quantifier holds.

title: expose node id via a.id or id(a)
description: Node id as a queryable property — currently `RETURN a.id` returns null because `id` is the node's storage id rather than a regular property. Downstream consumers need this to turn query rows into links without returning the whole node value and unpacking client-side.

title: Evaluate cstree as a rowan replacement (or other CST libs)
description:
Rowan has 5-year-old open UB issues and a maintenance pace that's not great for a launch-critical dep. cstree (domenicquirl/cstree) is the obvious alternative: fork of rowan, same core design (lossless CST, ThinArc-style thin pointers), but actively maintained, type-safe wrappers, built-in interning.

Goal: decide whether cyrs migrates from rowan to cstree (or another CST lib), or sticks with rowan + our upstream fix.

## What to investigate

1. **miri/SB status of cstree.** Run our miri rehash repro (phall1/rowan tests/miri_node_cache_rehash.rs) against cstree's equivalent API. If cstree passes miri standalone, it's a near-instant win.

2. **API delta vs rowan.** What cyrs touches in rowan:
   - GreenNode / GreenToken / SyntaxNode / SyntaxToken / SyntaxKind
   - TextRange / TextSize
   - NodeOrToken, WalkEvent, Preorder
   - GreenNodeBuilder + SyntaxTreeBuilder (in crates/cyrs-syntax/src/builder.rs)
   - Edit / replace_node / replace_range surface (crates/cyrs-syntax/src/edit.rs)
   Estimate the migration diff. cstree may require a SyntaxKind type with extra trait bounds (it uses  directly + a static interner mechanism).

3. **Maintenance signal.** Commit cadence, open issues, response times, latest release date. Compare honestly vs rowan.

4. **Performance.** Memory per node, build time, traversal speed. cstree claims slight overhead for the type-safety but should be in the same ballpark. cyrs has criterion benches at benches/* — port one to cstree and compare.

5. **Feature delta.**
   - rowan: thin pointer, mutable green tree builder, attached trivia model
   - cstree: ^ + type-safe AST wrapper generator, built-in interner, possibly arena-allocated nodes
   - Note any cyrs spec features (§4, §5) that depend on rowan-specific behavior.

6. **Other CST libs worth a paragraph each.**
   - cstree (primary)
   - tree-sitter (probably wrong shape — incremental parser, no passive CST)
   - biome/swc_common forks (probably too tied to JS world)
   - roll-your-own + text-size (multi-month, only if cstree disqualifies)

## Acceptance

- Written comparison doc (docs/evaluations/0001-rowan-vs-cstree.md or similar) covering the above.
- Recommendation: stay on rowan, migrate to cstree, or build custom. With effort estimate.
- If recommendation = migrate: file a follow-up bead with concrete migration plan. Don't migrate as part of this bead.

## Non-goals

- Don't actually migrate in this bead. This is decision-making only.
- Don't optimize for absolute perfection. A solid 'good enough' answer beats a perfect answer that takes a week to write.

Discovered: 2026-05-10 follow-up to cy-pom/cy-934 (rowan upstream engagement). The fact that we had to file two upstream PRs (#211 wasn't enough alone, needed our #212 on top) is itself a maintenance smell.
close_reason: Evaluated: cstree IS miri-clean for our repro (owned FxHashMap keys, no raw_entry_mut with borrowed ThinArc), but migration is 3500-5000 LOC across the workspace + 5 structural divergences (ownership flip on .parent()/.children(), Lang→Syntax trait restructure, resolver threading on every text() call, builder API return-shape change, salsa interaction unverified). Plus cstree has its own unsafe soup (no bug-class parity guarantee long-term). Recommendation: stay on rowan + upstream patches. Re-evaluate if rowan unmaintained-status escalates or cstree adds owned-navigation API.

title: Span↔byte-range helper: add TextRangeExt::as_byte_range (deduplicate inline conversions)
description:
There is no canonical helper in cypher-syntax for converting a TextRange to a std::ops::Range<usize> (or u32). Every consumer rolls its own:

Fix: add a TextRangeExt extension trait (or inherent helper) in cypher-syntax with:
- fn as_byte_range(self) -> std::ops::Range<usize>  // for slicing source &str
- fn as_u32_range(self) -> std::ops::Range<u32>     // for serde / lsp wire formats
- fn intersects(self, other: TextRange) -> bool     // dedup the duplicated 'ranges_intersect'

Also document in cypher-syntax's README + spec 0001 §4 the convention: cyrs uses byte offsets (not char counts, not lines/cols) for all spans; line/column conversion is owned by LineIndex in cypher-syntax and only happens at LSP/render boundaries.

Replace all the per-file rollups with the helper.

- All inline 'to_range'/'lsp_range_to_bytes'/'ranges_intersect' helpers deleted in favour of the trait

title: Crate naming triple-bind: dir vs package vs lib (cypher-syntax / cyrs-syntax / cypher_syntax)
description:
Every crate currently has THREE names that don't match:
- Directory: crates/cypher-syntax/
- Cargo package name: cyrs-syntax
- Rust lib name: cypher_syntax

Confusing for new contributors and a real footgun for crates.io publish (the README links 'cyrs-lang' on crates.io but no crate by that name exists yet).

Pick ONE convention and unify. Two viable options:

Option A — go all-in on cyrs-* (matches the project name, matches what cargo prints, matches the planned crates.io presence):
- Rename directories crates/cypher-* → crates/cyrs-*
- Update [lib] name = 'cyrs_syntax'
- Update all 'use cypher_syntax::' to 'use cyrs_syntax::' across workspace
- Update all docs/spec references

Option B — go all-in on cypher-* (matches existing source, smaller diff, matches the existing 'cypher' top-level crate and 'cypher' CLI binary):
- Rename Cargo packages cyrs-* → cypher-*
- Already matches dir name; lib name conversion is automatic
- Update workspace Cargo.toml [workspace.package] homepage/repo if they're cyrs-branded

Option B is the smaller diff but Option A is what the README and external docs already assume. Pick before publishing 0.1.0 — renaming a published crate is painful.

Acceptance:
- Single name per crate (allowing the standard hyphen→underscore Rust convention).
- 'cargo build' output and 'use foo::*' both reference the same name.
- crates.io publish list matches the README.

title: fuzz_plan: unresolved-variable assert fires from HIR→Plan lowering — bypassed name resolution
description:
fuzz_plan (libFuzzer, fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_plan.rs) panics in HIR→Plan lowering when fed input that produces an unresolved variable. The lowerer asserts that name resolution has already run, but the fuzz harness is calling lower_statement on HIR that bypasses that step.

Panic message:
  Unresolved variable `vaext` encountered in HIR→Plan lowering; run name resolution (cy-b4b) before calling lower_statement
  at crates/cypher-plan/src/lower.rs:1110:17

Reproducer:
- CI: gh run 25638947915, job 'fuzz smoke (5 min) / fuzz_plan (60 s)'
- Triggering commit: a8b688e (PR #37, branch feat/cy-eu2 — but the panic is independent of cy-eu2's formatter changes; fuzz_plan exercises the planner, not the formatter)
- Crash artifact name: crash-4032d9d4680ead1b8cfb8ced8e4c9f7cb078de70 (under fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_plan/ on the runner)
- Triggering input snippet (post-decode): `/1/ E001: unresolved variabl<bytes>e in WHERE (n {k:  vaext input re+uires the parserALL to produceE0500: un$1so$1lved var#abl<bytes>CH (n) WHERE missing\0\0r\0COUNT RETURN n\n`

Likely scope:
- Either fuzz_plan needs to invoke name resolution (cy-b4b) before lower_statement, mirroring how the real driver does, OR
- lower_statement needs to gracefully degrade (return Err) when handed unresolved HIR instead of panicking — this is what the bead description literally says ('run name resolution (cy-b4b) before calling lower_statement') so the planner already documents the contract; the fuzz harness is the violator.

Acceptance:
- fuzz_plan no longer panics on the saved crash input.
- Either fuzz_plan runs name resolution end-to-end, or lower_statement returns a recoverable error (preferred; harden the API contract in addition to fixing the harness).
- Add the crash input as a regression seed under fuzz/corpus/fuzz_plan/.

Notes:
- Discovered by the fuzz-smoke job which is continue-on-error: true (non-blocking), so this does not gate other work.
- This is the same pattern as cy-eu2 — a real fuzz finding from the same workflow run, just on a different target.
close_reason: Merged via PR #38; precheck recurses into PatternPredicate so unresolved names in pattern node-properties surface as Err instead of panic

title: fmt idempotency violation around // cypher-fmt: off escape
description:

  left:  '00// cypher-fmt: off

Os * absent ...'
  right: '00// cypher-fmt: off


Os * absent ...'
Identical otherwise; only an inserted '
' between the off-directive's trailing blank and the next token.

Scope:

Acceptance:
- New unit test in cypher-fmt asserts fmt(fmt(s)) == fmt(s) on a fixture containing '// cypher-fmt: off'.
- fuzz_formatter survives 60s of libFuzzer iterations on the reproducer without panicking.

- Discovered as a side-effect of PR #29 (fuzz-smoke target pin to GNU triple) — before that fix the fuzz build never reached the format step, so we were blind to this.

Acceptance:

- `echo 'MATCH (n) RETURN n' | cypher check` emits nothing and returns exit 0.
- Existing `tests/integration.rs` still passes; add one new test for the error path.
- `cargo xtask gate` clean.
close_reason: Verified already done. cypher-cli/src/main.rs uses Database (not LegacyDatabase), renders via cypher_diag::render_text_stderr, returns exit 1 on errors and 0 on clean input, threads --dialect through. title: rowan cursor::free SB UB: Box::from_raw races with sibling SyntaxNodeChildren iterator's retag
description:
Third distinct rowan miri SB violation (separate from #211 GreenNodeData and our #212 GreenTokenData fixes — both already stacked on phall1/rowan:fix/sb-node-cache-rehash).

Reproducer: with the rowan 0.16 bump + #211/#212 patches in place (cy-yrz branch), removing the cfg(not(miri)) gate from  in crates/cyrs-plan/src/lower.rs trips:



Root cause (read of rowan/src/cursor.rs from the fork branch):  does Box::from_raw(data) to drop a NodeData when its refcount hits zero, but a sibling SyntaxNodeChildren iterator holds an active SharedReadOnly retag covering the same [0x0..0x50] allocation. The retag was created from cyrs-hir/src/lower.rs:478 where we collect children via for_each.

Caught by: cy-yrz, after removing cy-863's miri gate.

Likely fix shape: cursor::free needs to release/invalidate the NodeData via raw-ptr drop_in_place + dealloc (skipping Box's drop, which adds the protected retag). Same family as our #212 fix but in a different code path.

Next steps:
1. File third upstream PR against rust-analyzer/rowan (after #212 lands, or stacked on top).
2. In the meantime: keep cyrs's cy-863 test gated cfg(not(miri)). Pointer to this bead in the gate comment.
3. Once upstream lands, drop the cy-863 gate and ship the follow-up.

NOT a v1 launch blocker — the test logic is verified at runtime; only miri (and only this specific test) flags the issue. The fmt path (cy-eu2) is fully unblocked by the existing #211+#212 stack.
notes: Strategy change: ChayimFriedman2 told us upstream rowan is being rewritten after rust-analyzer's assist migration, and is inclined to close PRs #211 + #212. Also noted that rowan passes Tree Borrows; SB rule we're hitting is unlikely to be in the final Rust aliasing model. = our 'UB' is academic miri-strictness, not real soundness. Reroute: patch cursor::free directly on phall1/rowan:fix/sb-node-cache-rehash branch (NO upstream PR), then cy-863's miri gate can come off. Smaller scope than originally planned.
close_reason: Fork patch shipped to phall1/rowan:fix/sb-node-cache-rehash (commit 9e7abd1). Replaced Box::from_raw with drop_in_place+dealloc in cursor::free + restructured to_next_sibling*/to_next_sibling_or_token to scope &mut NodeData borrow before free path (used existing dec_rc_raw helper). Regression test miri_cursor_free_sb passes; full cargo test clean. cyrs's [patch.crates-io] (PR #43 in flight) auto-picks up the commit. Gate removal in cyrs is a follow-up cyrs PR after #43 merges (cy-863 gate at crates/cyrs-plan/src/lower.rs:2100, ~3 lines).

title: Patch rowan-0.15 ThinArc SB violation in NodeCache rehash (upstream + use Cargo patch)
description:
Two fix sessions (cy-eu2, cy-863) hit a deterministic miri SB violation in rowan-0.15.18: rehash inside NodeCache calls GreenTokenData::text() which goes through HeaderSlice<GreenTokenHead,[u8;0]>::deref at arc.rs:264, and the SharedReadOnly retag on the tail slice fails because the borrow stack was invalidated by the prior reserve/insert. We've papered over it by gating parse-using tests under cfg(not(miri)), but each fix shifts allocation patterns enough to re-trip a different pre-existing test.

Upstream rowan is at github.com/rust-analyzer/rowan. Plan:
1. Fork rust-analyzer/rowan -> phall1/rowan.
2. Fix the SB violation in arc.rs / green/node_cache.rs — likely using std::ptr::addr_of! projections or raw-pointer arithmetic instead of &-reference Deref through the tail.
3. Add a miri smoke test in rowan that builds a tree large enough to trigger NodeCache rehash and runs cargo +nightly miri test. Verify the failure repros pre-fix and is gone post-fix.
4. Open PR in phall1/rowan against the fork's default branch (NOT against rust-analyzer/rowan upstream — user wants to review on their fork first).
5. After merge to phall1/rowan main, switch cyrs's Cargo.toml to a [patch.crates-io] override pointing at the fork; re-enable the cfg(not(miri))-gated tests; verify miri/cyrs-fmt + miri/cyrs-plan are green.

Reproducer (already in cyrs CI):
- gh run 25638947905 job 75256239232: miri/cyrs-fmt fails on corpus::snap_blank_line_between_statements with SB error in HeaderSlice deref.
- gh run 25639698954 job 75257867300: miri/cyrs-plan fails on lower::tests::match_where_inserts_filter with same SB error.

Acceptance:
- phall1/rowan PR open, with a miri test demonstrating the fix.
- (Follow-up bead, not this one) cyrs uses the fork via [patch.crates-io] and the cfg(not(miri)) gates around new tests can be removed.
notes: Superseded by upstream engagement (cy-934). Upstream PR #212 (https://github.com/rust-analyzer/rowan/pull/212) stacks on #211 and uses DST promotion (cleaner, smaller). phall1/rowan PR #1 (v0.15.18 backport, with_data callback approach) is still functional but probably not needed if we go the [patch.crates-io] → phall1/rowan:fix/sb-node-cache-rehash route.
